newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO CUP GAME WITH BARCELONA TO GO AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO CUP GAME WITH BARCELONA TO GO AHEAD.

text.p: Atletico Madrid's Spanish Cup quarter-final at Barcelona was set to go ahead on Wednesday after Atletico owner Jesus Gil changed his mind about pulling out of the competition.
Gil reversed his decision to withdraw his side from the match despite the news that the Spanish Football Federation had refused to annul suspensions imposed on three Atletico players.
He had originally suspended the trip to Barcelona because of the bans.
"There's no solution...the people who cause the grave damage will pay for it," said Gil, who is understood to be preparing legal action against the federation.

Argentine internationals Juan Eduardo Esnaider, Diego Simeone and key defender Delfi Geli were each suspended by the federation's disciplinary committee because of incidents in Atletico's 3-2 defeat at Real Betis on Sunday.
Atletico's bid to have the game replayed was also dismissed.
The cup holders were expected to fly to Barcelona this evening and travel straight to the Camp Nou stadium ahead of the 2130 local time (2030 GMT) kick-off.
A new element of disruption to the game emerged on Wednesday as public transport workers went on strike in Barcelona.

The strike may further aggravate a potentially tricky situation in the city where another cup quarter-final, between Espanyol and Las Palmas, is due to end shortly before Barcelona kick off against Atletico.
